verdicts.quote: Import commits account creation for a file as a single outcome. ... the admin finds no accounts created by that submission, even if some records were eligible.
Feedback identifies the offending record for a record-specific rejection. ... An admin told that a record failed validation can locate it in the submitted file from the feedback.
verdicts.missing: Whether one result lists every failing row with its reason, or reports only the first failure found.

verdicts.quote: include one account that already exists, the import reports the conflict and the original accounts keep their current details. / two otherwise valid records for the same new identity ... sees a duplicate conflict.
A caller supplies a role, permission, or other account setting they cannot assign through normal creation and the import refuses that assignment.
An admin allowed to create users can select and submit a CSV through the application's user-management experience.
verdicts.missing: Whether importing needs its own permission. The spec ties it to single-user creation permission rather than separating it.

verdicts.quote: An otherwise readable CSV omitting a required column is rejected with feedback identifying the missing column.
verdicts.missing: How unexpected or unknown columns are treated, and what happens when the header row is missing.

verdicts.quote: A quoted field containing a line break is treated as part of one record / the accepted text encoding
verdicts.missing: Which encoding is accepted, how a byte-order mark is handled, and whether CRLF/LF/CR line endings are accepted.

verdicts.quote: that user receives the corresponding communication after a successful import. / the admin finds no accounts created by that submission, even if some records were eligible.
A file with 1,001 otherwise valid user records is refused. / A CSV of 5,242,881 bytes is refused. / refused with feedback that identifies the exceeded limit.
A zero-byte file or a file containing only non-record content allowed by the accepted layout produces feedback that there are no users to import.
verdicts.missing: Whether a file with exactly one user record is accepted and handled like any other import.

verdicts.quote: If they resubmit the original CSV ... the import reports the conflict and the original accounts keep their current details. / If it had already completed, resubmission does not create duplicate accounts.
If ordinary creation under the same settings sends an invitation or other new-account communication to a user, that user receives the corresponding communication after a successful import.
verdicts.missing: Whether up to 1,000 messages go out at once, and any pacing or throttling.

verdicts.quote: An imported account enters the same setup state as an equivalent normally created account, including any existing activation or verification requirement.
Where normal user creation emits an audit record, the operator can find a corresponding creation record for an imported account with the information normally captured for that action.
verdicts.missing: An import-level record of who submitted which file and when. Only the existing per-user creation audit is kept.

verdicts.quote: After the admin resolves the cause of a prior rejection, they can submit an eligible CSV using the same import entry point.
verdicts.missing: Whether a running import can be cancelled, and how.

verdicts.quote: Existing callers submitting their usual single-user creation inputs continue to get the same results under the same permissions and settings. / Import leaves existing accounts untouched.
A record containing a value the normal creation path rejects for its format, length, or allowed values is rejected on the same basis.
verdicts.missing: How values that start with formula characters (=, +, -, @) are handled when echoed in results or exports, to prevent spreadsheet formula injection.
